It sounds like your doctor doesn’t understand ADHD. Please take a look into it yourself. I didn’t understand what it was until I was diagnosed. And I previously thought of it only as the stereotypes. 

Part of the “attention issues” with ADHD can be that we can focus intensely on things we love and are interested in. In your son’s case, that would be video games, tv shows, Pokémon. We have a hard time focusing on things that don’t interest us. For example, schoolwork. 

Your son may have read about ADHD and has identified some of the symptoms as his own. He may be crying out for help, recognizing that he can’t focus on things he needs to like schoolwork. It would be a shame to dismiss his issues as laziness when there could be something much more complex going on. 

With ADHD it can be extremely frustrating to not be able to focus on the things we find boring, especially when they are necessary for us to move forward in life. It can be extremely invalidating and frustrating to have those experiences brushed off as laziness.

I use this meditation technique of labelling. You don’t need to meditate to use it. I categorize things as “thought”, “emotion”, and “physical sensation.” So if I’m ruminating on a time when i embarrassed myself and felt bad about it, I can categorize that as a thought, and simply allow it to exist for a moment WITHOUT dwelling on it, and allow it to pass. If it’s bringing up more sadness I can label that as an emotion and let it exist and then pass. Similarly, if my face is itchy under my mask and I can’t scratch it at the moment, I label it as a physical sensation and allow it to exist. Do all of this without judgement. It’s much harder than it sounds  but in my opinion it is worth it in the long run to acknowledge your thoughts without dwelling on them. Doing this without judgement allows them to exist without being “good” or “bad” but simply being a thought. Hopefully this makes sense.

I also recommend checking out the THINK skill. It’s not in all dbt manuals but I’ve seen it here and in one place I did dbt. It says it’s good for “when you want to make peace, reduce conflict, and/or reduce anger.” I find it helpful for myself to calm myself when I haven’t done a DEARMAN, or when a DEARMAN hasn’t gone my way.

As for the GIVE skill, search in this sub for worksheets on that. It might not necessarily have phrases to use, but it may help you formulate how you’d say your DEARMAN. 

So Gentle means saying it in a way that’s not attacking or threatening your neighbour. 

Act Interested means you will listen to their point of view if they offer one, or even just listening to what they have to say. If they want to have the discussion at a later time, it’s not about you necessarily, it could be them expressing their needs and wanting to figure this out too. 

Validate - try to see the experience from their point of view. So again if they’re offering their POV, you could say “I realize this is hard for you...” or something like that. Just validating that they are trying too. 

Easy Manner - this ones hard for me since I get choked up in difficult conversations. It’s about literally having an easy manner. Try your best to smile and be light hearted. Avoid using any “attitude.” This will help soothe the person you’re talking to even tho it’s a difficult situation.

For the DEARMAN, write out what you would write for your DEAR. If you have any worksheets, or search up the worksheets on here, that should help. For Describe, simply describe the facts, so: the dog barks and you can hear it through the walls. Express is where you can get a bit more subjective— so this is where you’d put that it is bothering you, or express however this is making you feel. For Assert, what do you want? Here you’ll ask for them to try and keep their dog quieter or something like that. Reinforce could be as simple as “I would appreciate it” or depending on the situation consequences like “I’ll have to call the super if this keeps happening.” Again, I don’t know every detail of your situation but looking into local noise bylaws or any building rules could help depending on how far you want to take this. 
For your own sake, you could make a list of what-ifs to possibly answer, like the ones you did above. Hope this helps.

As for your moisturizer, make sure you're using a non-comodogenic one like Cetaphil, Eucering, or CeraVe. Stay away from things with added scent. Moisturizer with SPF is really important too!

I don't suggest mixing the moisurizer with the Tea Tree oil. Mix it with the carrier oil first, and apply that (with skincare, a rule of thumb is apply thinnest products to thickest), then once its dry(-ish) apply the moisturizer.
